analyzed_vuln.description: `__cil_insert_avrule` accepts 32-bit libsepol type/class values but stores `src`, `tgt`, and `obj` directly into the 16-bit fields of `avtab_key_t` without validating that they are in the representable, nonzero range. In this PoV an oversized source-type value is narrowed to zero (or otherwise wraps), and the malformed AVTAB entry propagates to neverallow checking. `check_assertion_avtab_match` then evaluates `p->attr_type_map[k->source_type - 1]`; with wrapped `source_type == 0`, this indexes before the allocation, and `ebitmap_match_any` crashes while reading the bogus `ebitmap_t`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The CIL input must expand/create enough primary type/type-attribute symbols that a type used as the source of an `allow` rule receives a policydb value beyond `UINT16_MAX` (the compact PoV achieves the large expansion through its block/inheritance structure). The rule must be emitted into the AVTAB and a matching-class/permission `neverallow` must remain enabled so assertion checking reaches the source bitmap lookup. The 32-bit source value is truncated when assigned to `avtab_key.source_type`; a value such as 65536 becomes zero, causing `attr_type_map[source_type - 1]` to access out of bounds.

args: Analyze the root cause and best error-handling fix for oversized or zero src, tgt, and obj values passed to __cil_insert_avrule in selinux/libsepol/cil/src/cil_binary.c. Identify the exact field widths of avtab_key_t, how this function's return value is propagated by every caller, whether there are existing constants/checks for maximum policy types/classes, and whether related insertion functions already validate representability.

The provided ASan report shows an oversized 32-bit source type narrowing to zero in avtab_key_t.source_type, followed by check_assertion_avtab_match indexing p->attr_type_map[k->source_type - 1] and crashing in ebitmap_match_any. The malformed value is generated by very large CIL block/inheritance expansion and an allow plus neverallow. We need patch only C/C++ under selinux, ideally reject all src/tgt/obj values not representable as nonzero avtab key fields before assignment and propagate a normal policy compilation error. I am inspecting __cil_insert_avrule and its callers now and want to ensure cleanup/error semantics and broader related paths are correct.

Explain the containing function, values assigned to source_type/target_type/target_class, error propagation possibilities, and whether a comprehensive root-cause patch should validate it along with __cil_insert_avrule, __cil_insert_type_rule, and __cil_avrulex_ioctl_to_hashtable.

We confirmed avtab_key_t has 16-bit source_type, target_type, and target_class. The reported crash occurs because __cil_insert_avrule takes uint32_t values and narrows an oversized source to zero. Searching cil_binary.c found analogous assignments at lines 983, 1272, 1697, and 3199. I want to avoid fixing only the known sink if line 3199 independently constructs malformed AVTAB keys. The intended strategy is a small shared validator for nonzero values <= UINT16_MAX, called immediately before every narrowing, with ordinary SEPOL_ERR propagation.
